query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the glass-forming ability and thermal stability of high-entropy alloys, with studies exploring the effects of composition, processing routes, and thermal treatments. The use of phosphorus as an alloying element has shown promise in enhancing glass-forming ability. Recent studies have also investigated the role of cooling rates on phase transformations and the development of amorphous structures.

The underlying mechanisms governing these properties are not yet fully understood, and further research is needed to optimize alloy compositions and processing routes.
